dse_runs.notes: Spec is suspected hard/infeasible: throughput_msps >= 400 AND max_abs_err <= 2^-12 at the same time. Map the boundary of the feasible region and keep the best-compromise designs (highest throughput at min error, and largest accuracy_bits at >=400 MSPS) so a selection can still be made if the feasible set is empty. Prefer unrolled/pipelined families for throughput.

final_text: The queue held a single spec, `infeasible_dds_400msps` (single-lane sin/cos at ≥400 MSPS with max_abs_err ≤ 2^-12 = 0.000244141, objective min LUTs / max accuracy_bits, selection by min LUTs, 400-eval L1 budget). I spent the budget exactly: `run_dse` used 200 evals and its inner architect declared the spec INFEASIBLE (refine → infeasible) with no feasible front, so I put the remaining 200 into the throughput-oriented families — 100 evals on `unrolled_k` (k clamped to the registry range 4..8; data_width 8..28, n_iter 4..30, angle_guard −2..4, frac_guard 0..4) and 100 on `pipelined_m` (m likewise clamped to 4..8) — both returning 0 feasible designs, and a further `explore_family` attempt was refused because 0 L1 evals remained. With no feasible design there was nothing to select, so `simulate_system` reported "nothing feasible to simulate yet", `verify_rtl` and `synthesize` reported "no selected design", and `back_annotate` was skipped (no winner change to flag, hence no `reexplore`); `finalize` therefore closed the spec with no design selected, 400/400 L1 evals used. All figures quoted are tool outputs (throughput/Fmax/LUT estimates from the cost model, M1 calibration; error exact from the golden model) — none were computed or invented by me, and the meaning is that the joint requirement of ≥400 MSPS single-lane throughput and ≤2^-12 error is not simultaneously achievable anywhere in the explored registry (iterative, unrolled_k, pipelined, pipelined_m), i.e. the accuracy constraint binds against achievable throughput even at maximum unrolling/pipelining. Lessons: k/m are clamped to 2..8 for unrolled_k/pipelined_m (beyond that is wasted exploration), and for suspected-infeasible specs the L1 budget is better spent early on max-throughput boundary points than letting the graph spend half of it re-declaring infeasibility.
